Description

Build validated detached snapshots for pure application tests.

No operation in this module contacts tmux. Named fixture references can model successive observations; they never equal a live Server generation. Snapshot and live-reference constructors remain hidden. Validation checks graph and metadata laws; wire decoding, tmux normalization and transport limits belong to acquisition rather than fixture construction.

Start with fixtureOrigin and emptyFixture, construct ordinary observation records using this module's reference builders, then call validateFixture.

Offline identity

data FixtureOrigin Source #

A named offline namespace. Equal names deliberately compare equal, so tests can model successive observations. This cannot represent a Server.

Complete fixture inputs

data Fixture Source #

Ordinary finite inputs. Validation applies the captured graph's laws; record construction or updates alone do not establish those laws.

data AttachedClient Source #

An attached client's native identity and context before graph validation. Validation resolves its values from the same snapshot; it never trusts a caller-supplied nested attachment record.

  • window :: !WindowId

  • index :: !WindowIndex

    Selected window-link index in the attachment session.

  • pane :: !PaneId

    The selected physical pane, not an independent client focus.

emptyFixture :: FixtureOrigin -> TmuxVersion -> Fixture Source #

Empty complete inputs with explicit synthetic metadata: PID 1, epoch 0 and path fixture:offline. No process or socket exists by implication. The version and every edited field are checked by validateFixture.

Validation

data FixtureError Source #

A failed graph or complete-snapshot validation, with domain context from the validator. Failed input never becomes an empty snapshot.

validateFixture :: FixtureOrigin -> Fixture -> Either FixtureError Snapshot Source #

Validate and force owned values using the capture graph's invariants. Successful fixtures have no acquisition interval and carry offline provenance. Their references cannot equal references from a Server scope.
